description: Nous sommes un groupe d'étudiants de l'Ecole Centrale Casablanca et nous participons à ce challenge pour apprendre davantage sur la vie dans l'espace, et nous challenger sur un sujet d'intérêt.
summary: HEXTA is an offline-first web app that helps astronauts monitor their own health on long missions, when no doctor is on board and the link to Earth is delayed or down. Every morning, a 90-second guided check-in records sleep, drowsiness, mood, symptoms and vitals, and explains how and why to take each measurement. HEXTA turns these entries into clear signals. For example, three short nights in a row alert the crew medical officer, with the evidence and step-by-step on-board guidance. When the link returns, a verified report reaches the ground with a receipt. HEXTA answers the challenge by guiding non-physicians through measurement, interpretation and action, on a phone, a tablet or a laptop. It matters because small warning signs must be caught early on the way to the Moon and Mars, and the same approach can serve isolated communities on Earth.
details:
What it does. HEXTA connects three roles:

  • The astronaut completes a short daily check-in, logs spot measurements (blood pressure, SpO₂, temperature, glucose) and reports symptoms with an optional photo.
  • The crew medical officer receives alerts, reviews the readings behind them, follows guided on-board steps, records a decision and requests a follow-up.
  • The ground receives only the reports the medical officer chooses to send.

How it works.

  • Offline first. Every entry is saved on the device first (IndexedDB), so the app keeps working without a connection.
  • Versioned rules. Rules evaluate the data. Our demo rule SLEEP-001 flags three consecutive nights under 6 hours and notifies the medical officer once, with the readings, their source and the rule version.
  • Sync. A persistent outbox syncs the data to a Laravel API backed by MongoDB Atlas when the link is available.
  • Verified reports. Reports are frozen and fingerprinted with SHA-256. The ground receiver stores each report once and returns a receipt. A resend returns the same receipt, and a different report with the same ID is rejected.
  • NASA data. Real astronaut data (NASA OSDR, Inspiration4 crew) is shown as historical context, never mixed with the simulated crew series.
  • 3D body. An interactive 3D body links each zone to the indicators tracked there.
  • Vision assistant (optional, Claude). It describes crew photos in plain words. Server rules stop it from naming a diagnosis, and it can only raise an alert, never lower one.

Benefits.

  • Catches drift (sleep, fatigue, symptoms) early, before it becomes an emergency.
  • Gives clear guidance to a medical officer who is not a physician.
  • Loses no data when the link drops, and never duplicates a report.
  • Runs as the same app on a phone, a tablet or a laptop.

What we hope to achieve. A foundation for an autonomous crew health tool for Gateway, the Moon and Mars, also useful for polar stations, ships and remote clinics.

Tools and languages.

  • Backend: Laravel 13 (PHP), MongoDB Atlas.
  • Frontend: TypeScript, Vite, Dexie/IndexedDB, service worker, Three.js.
  • AI: Anthropic Claude API (vision).
  • Tests: PHPUnit, Vitest, Playwright.
  • Demo video: ffmpeg, ElevenLabs.

Try it.

  • Live app: https://hexta-production-rj2n6h.laravel.cloud. Choose "Guided demo", then the Astronaut role, complete the check-in, then switch to the CMO role.
  • Project website (video, sources, 3D body): https://solene325.github.io/hexta-showcase/
  • Source code: https://github.com/Pierr26/Synergie_6
